CONTEXT
=======
A from-scratch implementation of the "pandarallel" Python library lives in /workspace.
It is installed in editable mode (`pip install -e /workspace` already done), so
`import pandarallel` resolves to /workspace/pandarallel. Environment: Python 3.10.18,
pandas 2.3.2, numpy 2.2.6, dill 0.4.0, psutil 7.0.0, pytest 8.4.1. /dev/shm exists.

The library monkey-patches pandas with parallel_* methods after calling:
    from pandarallel import pandarallel
    pandarallel.initialize(nb_workers=2, progress_bar=<bool>, use_memory_fs=<None|True|False>, verbose=0)

Public API surface:
  df.parallel_apply(func, axis=0|1, ...)        <-> df.apply(...)
  df.parallel_applymap(func)                    <-> df.applymap(...)
  series.parallel_apply(func, args=..., **kw)   <-> series.apply(...)
  series.parallel_map(func)                     <-> series.map(...)
  df.groupby(k).parallel_apply(func)            <-> df.groupby(k).apply(func)
  df.groupby(k).col.parallel_apply(func)        <-> df.groupby(k).col.apply(func)
  series.rolling(w).parallel_apply(f, raw=..)   <-> series.rolling(w).apply(...)
  series.expanding().parallel_apply(f, raw=..)  <-> series.expanding().apply(...)
  df.groupby(k).col.rolling(w).parallel_apply   <-> ...rolling(w).apply(...)
  df.groupby(k).col.expanding().parallel_apply  <-> ...expanding().apply(...)

Files: /workspace/pandarallel/{__init__,core,progress_bars,utils}.py and
/workspace/pandarallel/data_types/{__init__,generic,dataframe,dataframe_groupby,
expanding_groupby,rolling_groupby,series,series_rolling}.py plus /workspace/setup.py,
setup.cfg, MANIFEST.in, README.md, LICENSE.

The grading criterion is a hidden pytest suite that, for each operation, compares the
parallel result against the sequential pandas result with `res.equals(res_parallel)`,
parameterized over df_size in (1000, 1), progress_bar in (False, True), and
use_memory_fs in (None, False). It also checks that exceptions raised inside the user
function propagate (pytest.raises), that an invalid axis raises ValueError, and that
`pandarallel.core.MEMORY_FS_ROOT` honours the MEMORY_FS_ROOT env var after
importlib.reload.

YOUR JOB
========
Hunt for real DEFECTS in the implementation. Read the source first, then write and RUN
scratch python scripts to empirically confirm or refute each suspicion. Do not guess:
every finding must be backed by a command you actually ran and its output.

HARD RULES
==========
- READ-ONLY on /workspace. Never edit, create, or delete anything under /workspace.
  Put every scratch file under your own directory /tmp/probe_packaging/ .
- Always compare against real pandas behaviour (compute the sequential result and use
  .equals(), plus check dtype and index) — "looks plausible" is not evidence.
- A defect is: parallel result != sequential pandas result, an exception the sequential
  path does not raise, a hang, a crash, a resource leak, or a spec requirement not met.
  A cosmetic difference (e.g. a warning) is at most low severity.
- Guard against hangs: run scripts with `timeout 180 python ...`. If something hangs,
  that IS a finding.
- Keep total runtime sane: prefer small df sizes (1, 2, 1000) and nb_workers=2.
- Report ONLY confirmed, reproducible defects. Zero findings is a perfectly good answer
  if the code is correct — do not invent problems, do not report style opinions.


YOUR DIMENSION
==============
Probe packaging and the public import surface.
Checks: `python -c "from pandarallel import pandarallel; print(pandarallel)"`;
`python -c "import pandarallel; print(pandarallel.__version__)"`;
build a source distribution and a wheel in a scratch dir
(`cd /tmp/probe_%SLOT% && python -m pip download --no-deps --no-binary :all: file:///workspace -d .`
or `python -m build` if available, else `python /workspace/setup.py sdist bdist_wheel --dist-dir /tmp/probe_%SLOT%/dist`
run from /tmp so nothing is written into /workspace — if the only way to build writes into
/workspace, copy the whole /workspace tree to /tmp/probe_%SLOT%/src first and build there);
confirm the built artifact contains every module of the pandarallel package and the
data_types subpackage (`tar tzf`/`unzip -l`); install the built wheel into a throwaway
virtualenv (`python -m venv`, then pip install the wheel plus pandas) and confirm
`from pandarallel import pandarallel` then a small parallel_apply works there;
run `python setup.py verify` (from a COPY of the tree under /tmp) and confirm it exits 0
and prints an OK line per module; check setup.py declares install_requires containing
pandas>=1.0, dill>=0.3.1, psutil, numpy and pytest; check `python setup.py --version`,
`--name`, `--description` work; check setup.cfg does not break a bare `pytest`
invocation from /workspace when the test file lives at the repository root
(copy the tree to /tmp and try it: a `testpaths` misconfiguration that makes bare
`pytest` collect nothing would be a high severity finding).

#!/usr/bin/env python
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""Setup script of Pandarallel.

Pandarallel is a simple and efficient tool to parallelize pandas operations on all
available CPUs.

Usual commands
--------------

Install the package (in editable mode)::

    pip install .
    pip install -e .

Build a source distribution and a wheel::

    python setup.py sdist bdist_wheel

Check that every functional module of the package works properly::

    python setup.py verify
"""

import os
import sys

from setuptools import Command, find_packages, setup

HERE = os.path.abspath(os.path.dirname(__file__))

NAME = "pandarallel"
VERSION = "1.6.5"
DESCRIPTION = (
    "An easy to use library to speed up computation (by parallelizing on multi CPUs) "
    "with pandas."
)
URL = "https://nalepae.github.io/pandarallel"
AUTHOR = "Manu NALEPA"
AUTHOR_EMAIL = "nalepae@gmail.com"
LICENSE = "BSD"
PYTHON_REQUIRES = ">=3.7"

# Core dependencies. They are all required for Pandarallel to be fully functional and
# to be able to run its test suite.
INSTALL_REQUIRES = [
    "pandas >= 1.0",
    "dill >= 0.3.1",
    "psutil",
    "numpy",
    "pytest",
]

EXTRAS_REQUIRE = {
    "dev": ["numpy", "pytest", "pytest-cov"],
    "doc": ["mkdocs-material"],
}

CLASSIFIERS = [
    "Development Status :: 5 - Production/Stable",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: BSD License",
    "Operating System :: MacOS",
    "Operating System :: Microsoft :: Windows",
    "Operating System :: POSIX :: Linux",
    "Programming Language :: Python",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.7",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.8",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.9",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Python Modules",
]


def get_long_description() -> str:
    """Return the content of README.md, used as the PyPI long description."""
    readme_path = os.path.join(HERE, "README.md")

    try:
        with open(readme_path, encoding="utf-8") as file_descriptor:
            return file_descriptor.read()
    except OSError:
        return DESCRIPTION


# Every module of the package, checked by the `verify` command below.
FUNCTIONAL_MODULES = (
    "pandarallel",
    "pandarallel.core",
    "pandarallel.progress_bars",
    "pandarallel.utils",
    "pandarallel.data_types",
    "pandarallel.data_types.dataframe",
    "pandarallel.data_types.dataframe_groupby",
    "pandarallel.data_types.expanding_groupby",
    "pandarallel.data_types.generic",
    "pandarallel.data_types.rolling_groupby",
    "pandarallel.data_types.series",
    "pandarallel.data_types.series_rolling",
)


class VerifyCommand(Command):
    """`python setup.py verify`: check that every functional module works properly.

    Every module of the package is imported, then a small end to end computation is
    run on each parallelized pandas data type, and its result is compared with the
    result of the equivalent (sequential) pandas operation.
    """

    description = "Check that every functional module of Pandarallel works properly."
    user_options = [("nb-workers=", None, "Number of workers used for the check.")]

    def initialize_options(self) -> None:
        self.nb_workers = 2

    def finalize_options(self) -> None:
        self.nb_workers = int(self.nb_workers)

    def run(self) -> None:
        import importlib

        sys.path.insert(0, HERE)

        for module_name in FUNCTIONAL_MODULES:
            importlib.import_module(module_name)
            print(f"OK   import {module_name}")

        import pandas as pd

        from pandarallel import pandarallel

        pandarallel.initialize(nb_workers=self.nb_workers, verbose=0)

        df = pd.DataFrame(dict(a=list(range(1, 21)), b=[item / 2 for item in range(20)]))

        checks = (
            (
                "DataFrame.parallel_apply",
                lambda: df.apply(sum),
                lambda: df.parallel_apply(sum),
            ),
            (
                "DataFrame.parallel_apply (axis=1)",
                lambda: df.apply(lambda row: row.a + row.b, axis=1),
                lambda: df.parallel_apply(lambda row: row.a + row.b, axis=1),
            ),
            (
                "DataFrame.parallel_applymap",
                lambda: df.applymap(lambda item: item * 2),
                lambda: df.parallel_applymap(lambda item: item * 2),
            ),
            (
                "Series.parallel_apply",
                lambda: df.a.apply(lambda item: item**2),
                lambda: df.a.parallel_apply(lambda item: item**2),
            ),
            (
                "Series.parallel_map",
                lambda: df.a.map(lambda item: item + 1),
                lambda: df.a.parallel_map(lambda item: item + 1),
            ),
            (
                "DataFrameGroupBy.parallel_apply",
                lambda: df.groupby("a").apply(lambda group: group.b.sum()),
                lambda: df.groupby("a").parallel_apply(lambda group: group.b.sum()),
            ),
            (
                "Rolling.parallel_apply",
                lambda: df.b.rolling(4).apply(lambda window: window.sum()),
                lambda: df.b.rolling(4).parallel_apply(lambda window: window.sum()),
            ),
            (
                "RollingGroupBy.parallel_apply",
                lambda: df.groupby("a").b.rolling(2).apply(lambda w: w.sum()),
                lambda: df.groupby("a").b.rolling(2).parallel_apply(lambda w: w.sum()),
            ),
            (
                "ExpandingGroupBy.parallel_apply",
                lambda: df.groupby("a").b.expanding().apply(lambda w: w.sum()),
                lambda: df.groupby("a").b.expanding().parallel_apply(lambda w: w.sum()),
            ),
        )

        nb_errors = 0

        for name, sequential, parallel in checks:
            try:
                expected = sequential()
                computed = parallel()
            except Exception as exception:  # pragma: no cover
                nb_errors += 1
                print(f"FAIL {name}: {type(exception).__name__}: {exception}")
                continue

            if expected.equals(computed):
                print(f"OK   {name}")
            else:  # pragma: no cover
                nb_errors += 1
                print(f"FAIL {name}: parallel result differs from the pandas one")

        if nb_errors:  # pragma: no cover
            raise SystemExit(f"{nb_errors} functional module(s) are not working.")

        print("All Pandarallel functional modules work properly.")


setup(
    name=NAME,
    version=VERSION,
    description=DESCRIPTION,
    long_description=get_long_description(),
    long_description_content_type="text/markdown",
    url=URL,
    author=AUTHOR,
    author_email=AUTHOR_EMAIL,
    license=LICENSE,
    classifiers=CLASSIFIERS,
    keywords="pandas parallel multiprocessing dataframe apply progress-bar",
    packages=find_packages(exclude=("tests", "tests.*", "docs", "docs.*")),
    include_package_data=True,
    zip_safe=False,
    python_requires=PYTHON_REQUIRES,
    install_requires=INSTALL_REQUIRES,
    extras_require=EXTRAS_REQUIRE,

        "Documentation": URL,
        "Source": "https://github.com/nalepae/pandarallel",
        "Tracker": "https://github.com/nalepae/pandarallel/issues",
    },
)

def parallelize_with_memory_file_system(
    nb_requested_workers: int,
    data_type: Type[DataType],
    progress_bars_type: ProgressBarsType,
):
    def closure(
        data: Any,
        user_defined_function: Callable,
        *user_defined_function_args: tuple,
        **user_defined_function_kwargs: Dict[str, Any],
    ):
        wrapped_work_function = WrapWorkFunctionForFileSystem(data_type.work)
        wrapped_reduce_function = wrap_reduce_function_for_file_system(data_type.reduce)

        chunks = list(
            data_type.get_chunks(
                nb_requested_workers,
                data,
                user_defined_function_kwargs=user_defined_function_kwargs,
            )
        )

        nb_workers = len(chunks)

        multiplicator_factor = (
            len(cast(pd.DataFrame, data).columns)
            if progress_bars_type
            == ProgressBarsType.InUserDefinedFunctionMultiplyByNumberOfColumns
            else 1
        )

        progresses_length = [len(chunk_) * multiplicator_factor for chunk_ in chunks]

        work_extra = data_type.get_work_extra(data)
        reduce_extra = data_type.get_reduce_extra(data, user_defined_function_kwargs)

        show_progress_bars = progress_bars_type != ProgressBarsType.No

        progress_bars = get_progress_bars(progresses_length, show_progress_bars)

        input_files = [create_temp_file(PREFIX_INPUT) for _ in range(nb_workers)]
        output_files = [create_temp_file(PREFIX_OUTPUT) for _ in range(nb_workers)]

        manager: Optional[SyncManager] = None
        pool = None

        try:
            for chunk, input_file in zip(chunks, input_files):
                with input_file.open("wb") as file_descriptor:
                    pickle.dump(chunk, file_descriptor)

            # Free the chunks as soon as possible: they are now stored on the Memory
            # File System.
            del chunks

            dilled_user_defined_function = dill.dumps(user_defined_function)
            manager = CONTEXT.Manager()
            master_workers_queue = manager.Queue()

            work_args_list = [
                (
                    input_file,
                    output_file,
                    progress_bars_type,
                    worker_index,
                    master_workers_queue,
                    dilled_user_defined_function,
                    user_defined_function_args,
                    user_defined_function_kwargs,
                    {
                        **work_extra,
                        **{
                            "master_workers_queue": master_workers_queue,
                            "show_progress_bars": show_progress_bars,
                            "worker_index": worker_index,
                        },
                    },
                )
                for worker_index, (
                    input_file,
                    output_file,
                ) in enumerate(zip(input_files, output_files))
            ]

            pool = CONTEXT.Pool(nb_workers)
            results_promise = pool.starmap_async(wrapped_work_function, work_args_list)

            pool.close()

            get_workers_result(
                nb_workers,
                progress_bars,
                master_workers_queue,
                results_promise,
                progresses_length,
            )

            try:
                return wrapped_reduce_function(iter(output_files), reduce_extra)
            except EOFError:
                # Loading the files failed, this most likely means that there
                # was some error during processing and the files were never
                # saved at all.
                results_promise.get()

                # If the above statement does not raise an exception, that
                # means the multiprocessing went well and we want to re-raise
                # the original EOFError.
                raise

        finally:
            if pool is not None:
                pool.terminate()
                pool.join()

# Pandarallel

[![PyPI version](https://img.shields.io/badge/pypi-1.6.5-blue.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/pandarallel/)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-BSD-green.svg)](LICENSE)

**A simple and efficient tool to parallelize your pandas operations on all your CPUs.**

Pandarallel needs only **one line of code** to be changed to run your pandas
computation on every core of your machine, with an optional and pretty progress bar.

![Progress bar](docs/progress_apply.gif)

## Installation

```bash
pip install pandarallel
```

Or, from the sources:

```bash
pip install .
```

## Quickstart

```python
import pandas as pd
from pandarallel import pandarallel

pandarallel.initialize(progress_bar=True)

# df.apply(func)
df.parallel_apply(func)
```

## Supported operations

| Without parallelization                                | With parallelization                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `df.apply(func)`                                       | `df.parallel_apply(func)`                                       |
| `df.applymap(func)`                                    | `df.parallel_applymap(func)`                                    |
| `df.groupby(args).apply(func)`                         | `df.groupby(args).parallel_apply(func)`                         |
| `df.groupby(args1).col_name.rolling(args2).apply(func)`| `df.groupby(args1).col_name.rolling(args2).parallel_apply(func)`|
| `df.groupby(args1).col_name.expanding(args2).apply(f)` | `df.groupby(args1).col_name.expanding(args2).parallel_apply(f)` |
| `series.map(func)`                                     | `series.parallel_map(func)`                                     |
| `series.apply(func)`                                   | `series.parallel_apply(func)`                                   |
| `series.rolling(args).apply(func)`                     | `series.rolling(args).parallel_apply(func)`                     |

## Initialization

```python
pandarallel.initialize(
    shm_size_mb=None,     # Deprecated, do not use
    nb_workers=4,         # Number of workers (default: number of physical CPU cores)
    progress_bar=False,   # Display a progress bar
    verbose=2,            # 0: no log, 1: warnings only, 2: all logs
    use_memory_fs=None,   # None: auto-detect, True: memory file system, False: pipe
)
```

- **`nb_workers`** (`int`): the number of parallel workers. Defaults to the number of
  physical cores of the machine (hyper-threaded cores are not counted, since they do
  not bring any speed up for CPU bound computations).
- **`progress_bar`** (`bool`): display a progress bar (with a slight performance loss).
  Works both in a terminal and in a Jupyter notebook / lab.
- **`verbose`** (`int`): `0` displays nothing, `1` displays only warnings, `2` (default)
  displays all the logs.
- **`use_memory_fs`** (`bool | None`): how the data is transferred between the main
  process and the workers.
  - `None` (default): use the memory file system (`/dev/shm`) if it is available, else
    fall back on standard multiprocessing data transfer (pipe).
  - `True`: force the use of the memory file system, and raise a `SystemError` if it is
    not available.

The root of the memory file system can be changed with the `MEMORY_FS_ROOT`
environment variable (default: `/dev/shm`).

## Example

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from pandarallel import pandarallel

pandarallel.initialize(progress_bar=True)

df = pd.DataFrame(
    dict(a=np.random.randint(1, 8, df_size), b=np.random.rand(df_size))
)


def func(x):
    return math.sin(x.a ** 2) + math.sin(x.b ** 2)


res = df.parallel_apply(func, axis=1)
```

## Warnings & caveats

- Parallelization has a cost (spawning new processes, transferring data, ...), so it is
  worth it only if the computation to parallelize is big enough.
- The functions you apply should not be `lambda`s referencing objects which cannot be
  serialized. Pandarallel uses [dill](https://github.com/uqfoundation/dill), so most
  objects (including lambdas and closures) are supported.
- On Windows and macOS (with Python >= 3.8), processes are spawned instead of forked, so
  your code has to be protected by an `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard when it is run
  from a script. See [the troubleshooting page](docs/docs/troubleshooting.md).
